bodyHtml:
Short answer: UAE drug pricing after the Emirates Drug Establishment takeover is the federal list price EDE now sets and can cut, plus the separate payer listing that still sits with DHA, DOH and insurers. UAE launch research has to measure first price, repricing risk and who will fund the product after a list cut.

UAE drug pricing is a research problem again, not only a regulatory filing. On 5 January 2026 the Ministry of Health and Prevention transferred 44 core services to the Emirates Drug Establishment, including the re-pricing of individual medical products and the publication of regulated-medicine price lists (MOHAP, 5 January 2026). In May 2026 the same authority cut the retail prices of 168 chronic- and critical-care products (Gulf News, 26 May 2026). What a brand, HEOR or market-access team still cannot buy off the shelf is the first-price file the Drugs Pricing Committee will accept, which analog on that 168-product list can pull a net price, and which DHA, DOH or insurer wallet will fund the script after the list moves. This briefing uses only published sources. It sits alongside our healthcare market research hub and, for the payer-process map this page does not repeat, our UAE pricing and reimbursement strategy page.

Quick facts: UAE drug pricing and the EDE takeover, October 2026

  • 25–30 September 2023: Federal Decree-Law No. 28 of 2023 established the UAE Drug Corporation / Emirates Drug Establishment — issued 25 September, Official Gazette 29 September No. 760, effective 30 September (UAE Legislation).
  • 2 January 2025: Federal Decree-Law No. 38 of 2024 on medical products, pharmacists and pharmaceutical establishments came into force (UAE Legislation; Baker McKenzie, 14 January 2025).
  • 5 January 2026: MOHAP transferred 44 core services in full to EDE, including individual-product re-pricing and publication of regulated-medicine price lists (MOHAP).
  • 168 products had retail prices cut under EDE Decision No. 12 of 2026; published reductions ran from about 5% to nearly 60%, with Zocor 40 mg about 59.5% and Xalatan about 51.7% (Gulf News).
  • Two dates, one decision: Gulf News reported a 30 May 2026 pharmacy effective date; a legal-database listing of the same Decision 12 records issuance on 22 April 2026, Official Gazette No. 822 on 30 April 2026, and entry into force on 12 June 2026 (Gulf News; Eastlaws listing).
  • 20 pricing decisions in the first half of 2026, inside a half-year in which EDE approved 942 products and carried out 2,030 inspection visits (WAM, 22 September 2026).
  • 11.29 million residents in 2024, up 5.7% from 10.68 million in 2023 (FCSC Unified UAE Numbers).
  • 11.8% of adults 18+ had diabetes or were on diabetes medication in the last official published national health survey — a 2017–2018 figure, not a 2026 treated-share (MOHAP National Health Survey).

What is UAE drug pricing after the EDE takeover?

It is the federal public price the Emirates Drug Establishment now sets for a medicine that has marketing approval, the later decisions that can cut that price, and the commissioned work that tells a launch team whether a DHA, DOH or insurer committee will still fund the product after the list moves. It is not a syndicated UAE pharmaceutical market-size slide.

Report publishers such as Grand View Research, IMARC and IQVIA sell UAE pharmaceutical outlooks and audits. Those pages often occupy the query “UAE drug pricing”. Grand View Research, IMARC Group and IQVIA are useful for a first cut of national audit context. They do not say what country-of-origin certificate the Drugs Pricing Committee will accept, which analog on the 168-product list sits next to your brand, or whether a Dubai Drug Code or an Abu Dhabi wallet will carry the product after a cut. Those answers require a custom brief. Country context sits on healthcare market research in the UAE and UAE pharmaceutical market research.

A usable UAE launch research file after EDE usually needs:

  • A reconstructed first-price pack: country-of-origin certificate, Gulf and European reference prices, and the Decision 140/2013 mark-up path the committee still cites (EDE re-pricing card; Chambers Life Sciences 2026).
  • A dose-level map of every analog on Decision 12/2026 and a watch on the other published pricing decisions in the same half-year (Gulf News; WAM).
  • Payer and Pharmacy and Therapeutics interviews that treat DHA, DOH and private insurers as different decisions — the process map is on UAE pricing and reimbursement strategy, not in this briefing.
  • Arabic and English instruments, and sites in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and at least one northern emirate — not a Gulf average.

The unit of observation is the price certificate and the payer committee, not a vial forecast. Neighbouring systems are not a substitute. Compare healthcare market research in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait rather than importing an SFDA or MOH price into an EDE file.

What did the EDE takeover actually move?

The Establishment is older than the January 2026 service transfer. Federal Decree-Law No. 28 of 2023 created the UAE Drug Corporation — the English legislation title — on 25 September 2023, with Official Gazette publication on 29 September 2023 (No. 760) and legal effect on 30 September 2023 (UAE Legislation; Lexis Middle East). The EDE portal’s own Arabic copy says the Establishment was founded on 29 September (EDE portal). Use the legislation dates for legal effect. Use 5 January 2026 for the service transfer a launch team will feel in the filing queue.

Federal Decree-Law No. 38 of 2024 then replaced Federal Law No. 8 of 2019 on medical products, the pharmacy profession and pharmaceutical establishments. The UAE Legislation portal lists issuance on 1 October 2024 and effect on 2 January 2025 (UAE Legislation). Baker McKenzie’s 14 January 2025 note records a one-year grace period from that effective date and says the law was written to facilitate EDE’s take-over of responsibilities from MOHAP (Baker McKenzie).

The take-over that changed the filing address is the 5 January 2026 MOHAP statement. MOHAP wrote that it had transferred a set of services to EDE “to unify mandates, clarify institutional roles, and strengthen integration,” and that the restructuring included the full transfer of 44 core services, with EDE now solely responsible for their administration, regulation and oversight (MOHAP, 5 January 2026). The services named on that page include:

  • re-pricing of individual medical products;
  • registration and renewal of manufacturers of medical products;
  • certificates for pharmaceutical products intended for export;
  • renewal of registration for pharmaceutical products derived from natural sources;
  • publication of price lists for regulated medicines;
  • accreditation certificates for clinical studies or bioequivalence centres; and
  • certificates reflecting amendments to registered pharmaceutical products (MOHAP).

MOHAP’s companion list page tells applicants to submit the transferred-category requests through the EDE portal at www.ede.gov.ae (MOHAP service-list page). That is the operational meaning of “takeover” for a 2026 launch team: the price-list and re-pricing queue now sits at EDE, not at the ministry desk that used to issue the ministerial pricing decision.

Not everything moved. EnterpriseAM, reporting the ministry statement the next morning, wrote that some services were only “partially” transferred — facility licensing, advertising and emergency-drug approval described as still co-managed — and that narcotics and high-sensitivity controlled substances remained under the ministry (EnterpriseAM, 6 January 2026). NAVLIN Daily, on 12 January 2026, reported that the ministry keeps control of five key areas, including issuing prescription books for controlled medicine and approving narcotics for private hospitals (NAVLIN Daily). A launch brief that treats “EDE now owns all drug regulation” as a fact will mis-state a controlled-drug or advertising file. Split the 44 fully transferred services from the residual ministry list before you write the regulatory workplan.

EDE’s own first-half 2026 record, issued through WAM on 22 September 2026, is the first official activity count after that transfer: 2,030 inspection and regulatory visits by 30 June 2026, 828 non-compliant advertisements, 20 pricing decisions, 38 circulars, and 942 product approvals, of which 420 were conventional or biological medicines (63 of them innovator products), 376 healthcare products and 146 medical devices. Local manufacturing accounted for 247 UAE-made products — WAM’s phrase is “more than a quarter of the total” (WAM, 22 September 2026). Those are regulator activity counts. They are not a demand forecast.

The same WAM note is also the public record that EDE is now approving first-in-region and second-in-world products on compressed clocks. Foundayo (orforglipron) was approved on 3 April 2026, making the UAE the second country to register Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 for chronic weight management, with expected availability from May 2026 (WAM, 3 April 2026; WAM H1 note). WAM’s H1 wrap also names Inpefa (sotagliflozin) as a second-country approval, Baxfendy (baxdrostat) as a first-country approval, and EURneffy as the region’s first epinephrine nasal spray (WAM). Approval speed is not the same as a published public price, and a published public price is not the same as a payer listing. That gap is the research question.

How does UAE drug pricing get set and reset?

Article 20 of Federal Decree-Law No. 38 of 2024 is the current statutory sentence: marketing a medical product that has marketing approval requires a specific price, “determined in accordance with the general rules issued by a decision of the BOD” — the EDE Board of Directors (FAOLEX English text, Article 20). Article 36 creates a Pharmaceutical Policy Committee, reporting to the President, to propose policies on circulation, pricing and monitoring; the Cabinet is to decide its formation and working system (Article 36). Chambers’ 2026 UAE Life Sciences chapter repeats that EDE controls pharmaceutical and medical-device prices and that this committee is the dedicated policy body (Chambers).

The mark-up path that 2025 EDE pricing decisions still recite is older than EDE. Ministerial Decision No. 140 of 2013 unified the factory import price on a CIF basis in US dollars. Chambers describes Pharmacy Price as Import Price + 15%, then a public sale add-on of 28%, 24% or 20% of Import Price according to whether that import price is below AED 250, AED 250–500, or above AED 500, with EDE retaining discretion (Chambers Life Sciences 2026). Chairman’s Decision No. 49 of 2025 still lists Decision 140/2013 in its recitals (EDE Decision 49/2025 listing). The National’s 2013 report said retail prices of more than 6,600 medicines would be cut by up to 40% under that unification (The National). A first-price model still has to show that working. It is not a 2026 circular that republishes the arithmetic in English.

Re-pricing is a separate service with a published evidence list. The EDE card for “Re-Pricing of a Single Medical Product” tells the company to attach a country-of-origin pricing certificate that includes the proposed UAE price, to explain the justifications, and to supply reference prices from Gulf and European countries. The price is determined on the approval of the Drugs Pricing Committee. Fees are AED 1,000 for the re-pricing request and AED 500 for a new pricing certificate (EDE re-pricing card). Two research points sit inside that card. First, the comparator basket the committee is told to look at is Gulf plus Europe, not a global lowest-price screen the company invents. Second, the card still says a “ministerial decision” will then be issued. After 5 January 2026 the public price decisions in this briefing are Chairman-of-the-Board decisions, not ministry decisions (Decision 12/2026; Decision 49/2025). A launch file that still addresses the cover letter to the old ministry pricing desk is already out of date.

Chambers also records Cabinet Decision No. 90 of 2021 — the implementing regulation of the 2019 law, still in force to the extent it does not contradict Decree-Law 38/2024 — as providing that prices set by EDE or MOHAP may not be discounted or altered except by EDE or MOHAP themselves (Chambers; Baker McKenzie on residual 2019 regulations). That is why a “discount to win a tender” story is not a UAE private-pharmacy plan. The published lever after the takeover is an EDE pricing decision, not an off-invoice pharmacy cut.

Supply rules now sit in the same statute as the price. Article 22 requires the marketing-right holder to appoint at least two EDE-licensed pharmaceutical establishments as importers, to appoint one or more licensed distributors, to designate one main establishment for licensing, pharmacovigilance and lifecycle management, and to have all designated establishments actually carry out import operations during the calendar year (Article 22). Baker McKenzie notes that this continues the two-importer rule introduced by Law No. 11 of 2023 amending the 2019 law (Baker McKenzie). WAM’s H1 2026 wrap says that in February EDE approved a mechanism requiring companies to appoint more than one importer for each medical product marketed in the UAE (WAM). Marketing approval itself is valid for five years, with the renewal request due 90 days before expiry (Article 7). UAE launch research that stops at the price certificate, and never names the two importers or tests whether both imported last year, has not finished the access file.

What did Decision 12 of 2026 change on the shelf?

Decision No. (12) of 2026 is the first large, named EDE list-cut a 2026 launch team can put in a slide. Gulf News, updating on 26 May 2026, reported that EDE had reduced the retail prices of 168 pharmaceutical products across the UAE, covering cardiovascular disease, diabetes, hypertension, cancer, thrombosis and stroke, cholesterol disorders, gastrointestinal disease, psychological and neurological disorders, eye disease and asthma, in multiple dosages, and that pharmacies had already begun showing the revised prices. The same report said discounts ranged from approximately 5% to nearly 60% for some high-cost vital and biologic medicines, with Zocor 40 mg about 59.5% and Xalatan about 51.7% (Gulf News, 26 May 2026).

The published AED pairs in that report are the numbers a launch model can use. They are not a class average.

  • Cholesterol. Zocor 10 mg, 20 mg and 40 mg were unified at AED 67.50, from AED 83.50, AED 91.50 and AED 166.50 (Gulf News).
  • Glaucoma. Xalatan 0.005% fell from AED 89 to AED 43; GANFORT from AED 114 to AED 99.50; Combigan from AED 94 to AED 78.50 (Gulf News).
  • Oncology. Alunbrig 180 mg from AED 26,433 to AED 21,108; Alunbrig 90 mg from AED 19,824 to AED 12,520; Alunbrig 30 mg from AED 6,608 to AED 4,173; Xeloda 150 mg from AED 347 to AED 241 (Gulf News).
  • Heart failure. Verquvo 2.5 mg from AED 257 to AED 244; Verquvo 10 mg from AED 499.50 to AED 474.50 (Gulf News).
  • Type 2 diabetes. Amaryl 1 mg from AED 25 to AED 19; Amaryl 2 mg from AED 39.50 to AED 32; Amaryl 3 mg from AED 57.50 to AED 47.50 (Gulf News).
  • Hypertension. Renitec 10 mg from AED 64 to AED 48; Renitec 20 mg from AED 83 to AED 62; Aprovel 150 mg from AED 99.50 to AED 63.50; Aprovel 300 mg from AED 117 to AED 85 (Gulf News).
  • Anticoagulation. Pradaxa 110 mg from AED 220 to AED 198; Pradaxa 150 mg from AED 438.50 to AED 394.50 (Gulf News).
  • Psychiatry. Invega 3 mg from AED 449.50 to AED 381.50; Invega 6 mg from AED 562 to AED 381.50; Invega 9 mg from AED 843 to AED 416 (Gulf News).
  • Severe eosinophilic asthma. Nucala 100 mg vial and pre-filled syringe unified at AED 5,142, from AED 6,212.50 (Gulf News).

Two dates now sit on the same decision, and a launch file should keep both. Gulf News, writing on 26 May 2026, said the decision “will come into effect at the end of the current month (May 30)” and that pharmacies had already reflected the new prices (Gulf News). A commercial legal-database listing of Decision of the Chairman of the Board No. 12 of 2026 records issuance on 22 April 2026, publication on 30 April 2026 in Official Gazette No. 822, and a date of entry into force of 12 June 2026 (Eastlaws listing). This briefing has not inspected the Arabic Official Gazette page itself. The research instruction is: do not collapse a press-reported pharmacy date and a Gazette entry-into-force date into one cell. Ask the agency which date it used for “list in force,” and put the other date in the footnote.

Decision 12 is also not the whole 2026 pricing programme. WAM’s official H1 count is 20 pricing decisions, covering adjustments as well as reductions (WAM). A forecast that treats the 168-product cut as a one-off event, and does not watch the next Chairman’s pricing table, will be sent back the first time an analog moves again. The therapeutic spread in Decision 12 — diabetes tablets next to a lung-cancer TKI next to an asthma biologic — is the other warning. A chronic-care launch and an oncology launch are now in the same federal list-cut machine. They are not in the same payer committee.

Why a priced marketing authorisation is not access

EDE can approve a product quickly and still leave the funding question open. Foundayo is the clean example. WAM reported the 3 April 2026 approval, second-country status, expected May 2026 availability, and a 12.4% mean weight-loss figure at the highest trial dose (WAM, 3 April 2026). The same release quotes Director-General Dr Fatima Al Kaabi on obesity as an EDE priority because it is associated with more than 200 diseases and at least 13 cancers (WAM). None of that is a published public price, a Dubai Drug Code, or an insurer prior-authorisation rule. A launch model that converts “second country to approve” into “funded in May” has skipped the research.

The federal list price is one layer. Emirate payer listing is another. The hospital or insurer wallet is a third. This page does not repeat the DHA / DOH / MOHAP formulary walkthrough — that sits on UAE pricing and reimbursement strategy and on UAE market access research. What the published 2026 record adds is that the first layer has a new owner and a demonstrated willingness to cut 168 SKUs at once.

Insurance remains an emirate statute, not an EDE circular. Dubai Law No. 11 of 2013 makes health insurance mandatory in the emirate, including special development zones and free zones such as DIFC, and requires the entities named in Article 9 to enrol UAE nationals, residents and visitors (Law 11/2013). Dubai.ae states that employers, including free-zone employers, must cover employees, that sponsors must cover dependents, and that Dubai citizens and government employees are eligible under Enaya (Dubai.ae). The UNDP / Gulf Health Council NCD investment case describes Abu Dhabi’s Thiqa programme for UAE nationals, Dubai’s Saada programme, and employer-mandated cover for expatriate employees in both emirates (UNDP NCD investment case). A product can have an EDE public price and still sit outside the benefit design of a basic plan. That is a payer-research question, not a pricing-certificate question.

Two published lists now sit beside the EDE price list, and they are not the same list. EDE Chairman Decision No. 47 of 2025, dated 19 June 2025 and signed by Dr Thani Ahmed Al Zeyoudi as Chairman, adopted the UAE National Essential Medicines List (EDE legislations page; Decision 47/2025 PDF). WHO posted an English 2025 NEML file dated 3 June 2026 (WHO). In Dubai, General Circular 12/2018 defines the Dubai Drug Code list as every drug registered with DHA Pharmacy Services, with a unique code that already includes pack size and price (GC 12/2018). A molecule can be priced by EDE, coded in DDC, absent from NEML, or the reverse. UAE launch research has to say which list the forecast is using.

The treated population is also not the resident population. FCSC’s 2024 official estimate is 11.29 million residents, up 5.7% from 10.68 million in 2023, with about 200 nationalities (FCSC). The last official published national diabetes figure is 11.8% of adults 18+ from the 2017–2018 National Health Survey of 10,000 families, down from 18.9% in 2010 (MOHAP; UNDP). Decision 12 cut Amaryl 1 mg, 2 mg and 3 mg (Gulf News). That is not a 2026 treated-diabetes count, and it is not a DPP-4 or SGLT2 share. A diabetes or obesity launch that applies 11.8% to 11.29 million and calls it demand will be sent back. For the therapy-area design, see diabetes market research in the UAE and the 2026 context on UAE healthcare market trends 2026.

What should UAE launch research measure after EDE?

Design the study backwards from the decision — a first-price filing, a re-pricing request, a DHA or DOH listing, or a private-insurer prior-authorisation rule — not from a national market-size slide.

WorkstreamDecision it answersWhat the published record already showsWhat to commission
First-price fileWhat the committee can acceptArticle 20 ties the price to EDE Board rules; the EDE re-pricing card still asks for a country-of-origin certificate plus Gulf and European references (Decree-Law 38/2024; EDE re-pricing card)Rebuild the certificate and the comparator basket before first filing
List-cut exposureWhich analog can pull the netDecision 12/2026 cut 168 products; Zocor 40 mg about 59.5% and Xalatan about 51.7% (Gulf News, 26 May 2026)Dose-level analog map plus a watch on the other 19 H1 pricing decisions
Dual importerWho can land the stockArticle 22 requires at least two importers; WAM says EDE approved a multi-importer mechanism in February 2026 (Article 22; WAM)Name both importers and test whether both imported in the last calendar year
Payer listingWho funds the scriptDubai Law 11/2013 makes insurance mandatory in Dubai, including free zones; DDC codes carry a price field (Law 11/2013; GC 12/2018)Separate DHA, DOH and insurer interviews — see UAE pricing and reimbursement strategy
Treated-patient shareWhat happens after the cutDiabetes in the last published national survey was 11.8% of adults 18+ — a prevalence, not a treated share (MOHAP National Health Survey)Anonymous PRFs, new versus continuing, by emirate and specialty

The table and the seven-workstream figure are the brief. Two extra research notes sit outside the rows. First, WAM’s note that Novo Nordisk will put a regional distribution centre in the UAE to serve up to 70 countries is a logistics fact, not a substitute for the two named Article 22 importers (WAM; Article 22). Second, Foundayo’s second-country approval on 3 April 2026 and May 2026 availability statement are published (WAM); an oral-GLP-1 file still has to produce a first-price pack, a dual-importer map and plan-specific obesity-cover interviews. It should not invent an EDE public price that is not on a current list. HEOR design for a class-level budget impact sits on GCC pharmacoeconomics and real-world evidence in the GCC.

How should you commission the study?

  • How many pricing-committee-adjacent, DHA, DOH and insurer respondents will you recruit, and from which emirates — Dubai, Abu Dhabi and at least one northern emirate?
  • Will results be reported by public versus private channel, by nationality, and by new versus current treated patients?
  • Which Decision 12 analogs, and which of the other H1 2026 pricing decisions, sit in the discussion guide?
  • Will the first-price reconstruction show the country-of-origin certificate, the Gulf/Europe basket, and the Decision 140/2013 path as three workings, not one “UAE price”?
  • Are questionnaires available in Arabic and English?
  • Who owns the data, and can it be re-cut after the next Chairman’s pricing table?

Desk-research market-size reports remain useful for a first cut of audit context. Grand View Research, IMARC and IQVIA publish UAE pharmaceutical pages that often appear for this query. Use them to triangulate national spend. Do not take them to an EDE pricing committee or a DHA listing meeting as the evidence pack for a first price or a list-cut response.

A physician-survey design that is siblinged to Saudi work should still keep the samples separate — see GLP-1 physician survey methods in Saudi Arabia for the instrument discipline, not for the UAE price. For the vendor comparison, see top healthcare market research companies in the UAE 2026 and pharmaceutical companies in the UAE.

Why choose BioNixus for UAE launch research after the EDE takeover?

BioNixus is a primary market research and market access consultancy for pharmaceutical, medical device and healthcare companies, founded in 2012. It has served 118 clients in 48 countries, has run 127 studies so far in 2026 and works with a network of 82,000+ physicians globally and about 3,200 physicians in the Middle East. Custom study pricing is typically $10k–$60k. Regional leadership offices are in Sheridan, Wyoming (US headquarters), London EC1V 2NX and Cairo (Sheikh Zayed, Giza). Dubai, Al Khobar and Salmiya, Kuwait (Olympia Mall) are field offices, and São Paulo is a field office for LATAM. LATAM work is covered from the US office with a strong local consultant network.

Choose BioNixus when the decision depends on why EDE, DHA, DOH and insurer medical directors will accept a first price or absorb a list cut, rather than on a syndicated UAE pharmaceutical total. Each study is built around one decision — a pricing certificate, a re-pricing request, a listing or a prior-authorisation rule — and is reported as share of treated patients. The delivery commitment is Guaranteed in writing. That guarantee covers the agreed scope and timeline, not the accuracy of findings. Where reviews are relevant, BioNixus has 40 client reviews. The written guarantees are: replace non-qualifying respondents at no charge; a minimum sample; re-field at our cost if agreed quotas are missed; and a pilot fee credited to the main field.

See also healthcare market research in the UAE, UAE pricing and reimbursement strategy, UAE market access research and the 2026 UAE healthcare market research ranking.

body.title: Short answer
body.content: UAE drug pricing after the Emirates Drug Establishment takeover is the federal list price EDE now sets and can cut, plus the separate payer listing that still sits with DHA, DOH and insurers. UAE launch research has to measure first price, repricing risk and who will fund the product after a list cut.

children.text: It sits alongside our healthcare market research hub and, for the payer-process map this page does not repeat, our UAE pricing and reimbursement strategy page. Quick facts: UAE drug pricing and the EDE takeover, October 2026 25–30 September 2023: Federal Decree-Law No. 28 of 2023 established the UAE Drug Corporation / Emirates Drug Establishment — issued 25 September, Official Gazette 29 September No. 760, effective 30 September ( UAE Legislation ). 2 January 2025: Federal Decree-Law No. 38 of 2024 on medical products, pharmacists and pharmaceutical establishments came into force ( UAE Legislation ; Baker McKenzie, 14 January 2025 ). 5 January 2026: MOHAP transferred 44 core services in full to EDE, including individual-product re-pricing and publication of regulated-medicine price lists ( MOHAP ). 168 products had retail prices cut under EDE Decision No. 12 of 2026; published reductions ran from about 5% to nearly 60%, with Zocor 40 mg about 59.5% and Xalatan about 51.7% ( Gulf News ). Two dates, one decision: Gulf News reported a 30 May 2026 pharmacy effective date; a legal-database listing of the same Decision 12 records issuance on 22 April 2026, Official Gazette No. 822 on 30 April 2026, and entry into force on 12 June 2026 ( Gulf News ; Eastlaws listing ). 20 pricing decisions in the first half of 2026, inside a half-year in which EDE approved 942 products and carried out 2,030 inspection visits ( WAM, 22 September 2026 ). 11.29 million residents in 2024, up 5.7% from 10.68 million in 2023 ( FCSC Unified UAE Numbers ). 11.8% of adults 18+ had diabetes or were on diabetes medication in the last official published national health survey — a 2017–2018 figure, not a 2026 treated-share ( MOHAP National Health Survey ).

faq.question: What is UAE drug pricing after the EDE takeover?
faq.answer: UAE drug pricing after the EDE takeover is the federal public price the Emirates Drug Establishment now sets for a medicine that has marketing approval, plus the later decisions that can cut that price. MOHAP transferred 44 core services, including individual-product re-pricing and publication of regulated-medicine price lists, to EDE on 5 January 2026. A priced marketing authorisation is not DHA, DOH or insurer listing.

faq.question: When did the Emirates Drug Establishment take over drug pricing from MOHAP?
faq.answer: EDE was established by Federal Decree-Law No. 28 of 2023 (issued 25 September 2023, effective 30 September 2023). Federal Decree-Law No. 38 of 2024, in force on 2 January 2025, gave the EDE Board the power to set the pricing rules. The filing-address change is the 5 January 2026 MOHAP transfer of 44 services, including re-pricing and price-list publication.

faq.question: What did EDE Decision 12 of 2026 change?
faq.answer: Decision No. 12 of 2026 reduced retail prices of 168 pharmaceutical products used for chronic and critical illnesses. Gulf News reported reductions from about 5% to nearly 60%, with Zocor 40 mg about 59.5% and Xalatan about 51.7%, and a pharmacy effective date of 30 May 2026. A legal-database listing of the same decision records Official Gazette publication on 30 April 2026 and entry into force on 12 June 2026. Keep both dates in the file.

faq.question: Is a UAE EDE price the same as reimbursement?
faq.answer: No. Article 20 of Decree-Law 38/2024 requires a specific EDE-set price before marketing. Dubai Law 11 of 2013 and Abu Dhabi’s Thiqa / employer rules still decide who pays. DHA’s Dubai Drug Code and EDE’s 2025 National Essential Medicines List are separate lists. Commission payer interviews; do not treat the federal list price as a listing.

faq.question: What evidence does EDE ask for to re-price a medicine?
faq.answer: The published EDE re-pricing card asks for a country-of-origin pricing certificate that includes the proposed UAE price, written justifications, and reference prices from Gulf and European countries. The Drugs Pricing Committee approves the price. Fees are AED 1,000 for the request and AED 500 for a new pricing certificate. After January 2026 the public decision is an EDE Chairman’s decision, even if older cards still say “ministerial”.

faq.question: What should UAE launch research measure in 2026?
faq.answer: UAE launch research should reconstruct the first-price file, map Decision 12 analogs and later pricing decisions, name the two Article 22 importers, interview DHA, DOH and insurer medical directors separately, measure treated-patient share rather than census prevalence, and test budget impact after a list cut. A syndicated UAE pharmaceutical market-size report does not answer those questions.

faq.question: Why commission BioNixus for UAE launch research after the EDE takeover?
faq.answer: BioNixus runs custom primary research from a Dubai field office, with a network of 82,000+ physicians globally and about 3,200 physicians in the Middle East, and prices typical custom studies at $10k–$60k. The work is designed around one decision — a pricing certificate, a re-pricing request or a listing — and reported as share of treated patients. The delivery commitment is Guaranteed in writing. That guarantee covers scope and timeline, not findings.
